Elevator: the choices to defend, and the follow-ups to expect

The demo's last call shows why dispatch must be swappable: under zoning, car A travels from floor 8 to floor 1 while car B sits idle one floor away. Zoning wins at 9 a.m., when everyone comes from the lobby, and loses at 3 p.m. Interviewers want you to say which rule fits which traffic, then show the rule is one class.

DecisionWhy, and the alternative
Dispatch as a strategyThe rule changes with traffic and time of day; the cars do not. Swapped at runtime by useDispatcher.
LOOK inside the carRouting uses only the car's own stops, so it belongs to the car (information expert).
Hall calls assigned onceSimple and predictable. Real controllers re-assign pending calls every few seconds as cars move; a follow-up.
Discrete ticksDeterministic and testable. A real system is event-driven, with timers for travel and doors.
Arrivals as eventsDisplays, chimes and logs subscribe. The car does not know about any of them.
One lock on the systemButton presses, ticks and strategy swaps all serialise. At a few events per second that costs nothing, and it rules out a car being given a stop mid-step.
The listener runs inside the lockIn the demo a listener presses a car button from inside tick, which works because Java's intrinsic locks are re-entrant. A slow listener (a network call to a display) would hold up every car, though. In production, publish events to a queue and let listeners consume them on another thread. It is the same trade-off as synchronous and asynchronous observers.
Follow-upWhat changes
Honour hall-call directionKeep up-stops and down-stops in separate sets; a car serves a floor on the way up only for an up call. step reads the set for its current direction. The dispatcher already accounts for it.
CapacityEach car tracks its load; the dispatcher skips full cars, and a full car ignores hall-call stops until riders get out.
A car out of serviceA serviceable flag, or a State for the car. The dispatcher filters it out; its pending hall calls are handed back to the dispatcher.
Destination dispatchRiders enter their floor in the lobby, so a hall call carries its destination. The dispatcher groups riders by destination, and returns which car to wait for.
Rush-hour switchingA ScheduledDispatcher that delegates to zoning or nearest-car by time of day: a strategy that picks a strategy. No other class changes.
Fire modeA system-wide state: every car cancels its stops and returns to the lobby, and hall calls are refused.

Movie booking: many users, one seat map, and a hold that must expire

BookMyShow-style booking is the LLD problem where concurrency is the requirement, not a follow-up. Two people clicking the same seat at the same moment must not both get it. A user who selects seats and walks away must not block them forever. Payment takes time, and the hold can run out while it happens.

Functional requirements

  1. A show is a movie on a screen at a start time. Its seats have a category: regular, premium or recliner.
  2. A user selects one or more seats and gets a hold on all of them, or on none. A partial hold is never created.
  3. A hold lasts 8 minutes. After that the seats are free for anyone, without waiting for a cleanup job.
  4. The price is the category's base price, +25% on weekends, and must be changeable.
  5. Paying confirms the booking. If the hold expired while the payment was in progress, the payment is refunded and the booking fails.
  6. A user can cancel a hold before paying; the seats are released at once.
  7. Anyone can see the seat map: free, held or sold.

Questions to ask first

How many users on one show?
Hundreds at release time, all hitting the same seats. Design for contention.
Cities, theatres, search?
Catalogue browsing is out of scope; start from a show.
Cancelling a paid booking?
A follow-up, with a refund policy.
Payment provider?
Behind an interface; it can be slow or fail.
Seat rules (no single gaps)?
Not now. It is a good follow-up.

Nouns, and what they become

BookingService · facadeShowBooking Seat · recordMovie · recordSeatCategory · enumBookingStatus · enum PricingStrategyPaymentGateway

Not classes here: theatre, city, screen (the seat layout is all the show needs), user (an id), ticket (a confirmed booking).

Say the concurrency plan in the first ten minutes"Each seat of a show is claimed atomically; a multi-seat hold claims them in a fixed order and rolls back on the first conflict. Expiry is checked when someone wants the seat, so no job is needed for correctness." Interviewers want to hear this before the class diagram.

Movie booking: the show owns who holds each seat, the booking owns its own lifecycle

Seat ownership lives in one concurrent map per show: seat to booking id. A seat is free when it has no entry, or when its booking has expired or been cancelled. The booking decides, under its own lock, whether it is still alive. The service is a facade that coordinates the two with pricing and payment.

BookingService facade - bookings : ConcurrentMap<id, Booking> - pricing : PricingStrategy - payments : PaymentGateway - clock : Clock + hold(user, Show, seats) : Optional<Booking> + confirm(bookingId) : Booking + cancel(bookingId) + seatMap(Show) : String ──> PricingStrategy ──> PaymentGateway ◆── * Booking Show - id - movie : Movie - start : LocalDateTime - seats : SortedMap<label, Seat> - claims : ConcurrentMap<Seat, bookingId> + claim(Seat, id) : boolean putIfAbsent + reclaim(Seat, fromId, toId) : boolean replace: CAS + release(Seat, id) remove(key, value) Booking synchronized methods - id - user - seats : List<Seat> - amount - heldUntil : Instant - status : BookingStatus + tryConfirm(now, paymentRef) : boolean + tryExpire(now) : boolean true: its seats may go + cancel() : boolean «record» Seat row, number, category Comparable «enum» SeatCategory REGULAR 200, PREMIUM 350, RECLINER 600 «enum» BookingStatus HELD, CONFIRMED, EXPIRED, CANCELLED
Booking lifecycle HELD ──tryConfirm, before heldUntil──> CONFIRMED HELD ──tryExpire, after heldUntil───> EXPIRED HELD ──cancel──────────────────────> CANCELLED CONFIRMED, EXPIRED and CANCELLED are final
ClassOwns the decision
ShowWhich booking holds each seat, changed only by atomic map operations
BookingWhether it is still alive, and the single transition out of HELD
BookingServiceAll-or-nothing holds, the payment sequence, refunds
PricingStrategyWhat a seat costs for this show
Why the map stores ids, not bookingsThe claim map needs only an identity to compare and swap. ConcurrentHashMap.replace(seat, oldId, newId) compares with equals, so it succeeds only if the seat still belongs to the dead booking. Storing ids also keeps the show free of any reference to payments or users.

Movie booking: atomic seat claims on the show, one-way transitions on the booking

The show exposes exactly three ways to change a seat's owner, and each is a single atomic call on ConcurrentHashMap. The booking's transitions are synchronized and each checks the clock. So "confirm" and "expire" can never both succeed on the same booking, whichever thread gets there first.

BookingDemo.java · 1 of 3 · the model
import java.time.*;
import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;

enum SeatCategory {
    REGULAR(200), PREMIUM(350), RECLINER(600);
    final long basePrice;
    SeatCategory(long basePrice) { this.basePrice = basePrice; }
}

record Seat(char row, int number, SeatCategory category) implements Comparable<Seat> {
    private static final Comparator<Seat> ORDER =
            Comparator.comparing(Seat::row).thenComparingInt(Seat::number);
    public int compareTo(Seat other) { return ORDER.compare(this, other); }
    @Override public String toString() { return "" + row + number; }
}

record Movie(String title, int minutes) {}

final class Show {
    private final String id;
    private final Movie movie;
    private final LocalDateTime start;
    private final SortedMap<String, Seat> seats = new TreeMap<>();
    private final ConcurrentMap<Seat, String> claims = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    Show(String id, Movie movie, LocalDateTime start, Map<Character, SeatCategory> rows, int perRow) {
        this.id = id; this.movie = movie; this.start = start;
        rows.forEach((row, cat) -> {
            for (int n = 1; n <= perRow; n++) seats.put("" + row + n, new Seat(row, n, cat));
        });
    }
    String id() { return id; }
    Movie movie() { return movie; }
    LocalDateTime start() { return start; }
    Collection<Seat> seats() { return seats.values(); }
    Seat seat(String label) {
        Seat s = seats.get(label);
        if (s == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no seat " + label);
        return s;
    }

    String claimant(Seat s) { return claims.get(s); }
    boolean claim(Seat s, String bookingId) { return claims.putIfAbsent(s, bookingId) == null; }
    boolean reclaim(Seat s, String fromId, String toId) { return claims.replace(s, fromId, toId); }
    void release(Seat s, String bookingId) { claims.remove(s, bookingId); }  // only if still ours
}

enum BookingStatus { HELD, CONFIRMED, EXPIRED, CANCELLED }

final class Booking {
    private final String id, user;
    private final Show show;
    private final List<Seat> seats;
    private final long amount;
    private final Instant heldUntil;
    private BookingStatus status = BookingStatus.HELD;
    private String paymentRef;

    Booking(String id, String user, Show show, List<Seat> seats, long amount, Instant heldUntil) {
        this.id = id; this.user = user; this.show = show;
        this.seats = List.copyOf(seats); this.amount = amount; this.heldUntil = heldUntil;
    }
    String id() { return id; }
    String user() { return user; }
    Show show() { return show; }
    List<Seat> seats() { return seats; }
    long amount() { return amount; }
    synchronized BookingStatus status() { return status; }

    synchronized boolean tryConfirm(Instant now, String ref) {
        if (status == BookingStatus.HELD && !now.isBefore(heldUntil)) status = BookingStatus.EXPIRED;
        if (status != BookingStatus.HELD) return false;
        status = BookingStatus.CONFIRMED;
        paymentRef = ref;
        return true;
    }

    synchronized boolean tryExpire(Instant now) {      // may its seats be taken?
        if (status == BookingStatus.HELD && !now.isBefore(heldUntil)) status = BookingStatus.EXPIRED;
        return status == BookingStatus.EXPIRED || status == BookingStatus.CANCELLED;
    }

    synchronized boolean isLive(Instant now) {         // for display only
        return status == BookingStatus.HELD && now.isBefore(heldUntil);
    }

    synchronized boolean cancel() {
        if (status != BookingStatus.HELD) return false;
        status = BookingStatus.CANCELLED;
        return true;
    }

    @Override public synchronized String toString() {
        return id + " " + user + " " + seats + " " + amount + " " + status
                + (paymentRef == null ? "" : " " + paymentRef);
    }
}
Three atomic operations, nothing elseputIfAbsent claims a free seat. replace(seat, old, new) takes a seat from a dead booking only if it still belongs to that booking. remove(seat, id) releases a seat only if it is still ours, so a late cancel cannot free a seat someone else has since claimed. There is no check-then-act anywhere, so there is no race window.
Why expiry is lazyA hold is dead the moment its time passes, whether or not anything noticed. tryExpire records that when a competing user asks for the seat. A cleanup job can still sweep old holds to tidy the map, but correctness never depends on it running on time.
Why Seat is ComparableA multi-seat hold claims seats in sorted order. If two users hold {A1, A2} and {A2, A1} and each claimed in the order given, each could get one seat and fail on the other. Both would then roll back, and could keep doing so under load. A fixed order, the same idea that prevents deadlocks, makes one of them win outright.

Movie booking: all-or-nothing holds, a race of 100 users, and a payment that outlives its hold

hold registers the booking, then claims each seat in order, taking seats from dead bookings with a compare-and-swap. The first live conflict releases everything claimed so far. confirm charges first and confirms second, because confirming is instant and charging is not. If the hold ran out in between, it refunds.

BookingDemo.java · 2 of 3 · pricing, payment and the booking service
interface PricingStrategy { long price(Show show, Seat seat); }

final class WeekendPricing implements PricingStrategy {
    public long price(Show show, Seat seat) {
        DayOfWeek d = show.start().getDayOfWeek();
        boolean weekend = d == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY || d == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY;
        return weekend ? seat.category().basePrice * 125 / 100 : seat.category().basePrice;
    }
}

interface PaymentGateway {
    String charge(String user, long amount);
    void refund(String ref);
}

final class BookingService {
    private static final Duration HOLD = Duration.ofMinutes(8);
    private final ConcurrentMap<String, Booking> bookings = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final AtomicInteger nextId = new AtomicInteger(1);
    private final PricingStrategy pricing;
    private final PaymentGateway payments;
    private final Clock clock;

    BookingService(PricingStrategy pricing, PaymentGateway payments, Clock clock) {
        this.pricing = pricing; this.payments = payments; this.clock = clock;
    }

    Optional<Booking> hold(String user, Show show, List<String> labels) {
        List<Seat> seats = labels.stream().map(show::seat).distinct().sorted().toList();
        long amount = seats.stream().mapToLong(s -> pricing.price(show, s)).sum();
        var b = new Booking("BK" + nextId.getAndIncrement(), user, show, seats,
                            amount, clock.instant().plus(HOLD));
        bookings.put(b.id(), b);                  // visible before it claims
        List<Seat> claimed = new ArrayList<>();
        for (Seat s : seats) {
            if (!claimSeat(show, s, b.id())) {    // all or nothing
                claimed.forEach(c -> show.release(c, b.id()));
                b.cancel();
                bookings.remove(b.id());
                return Optional.empty();
            }
            claimed.add(s);
        }
        return Optional.of(b);
    }

    private boolean claimSeat(Show show, Seat seat, String id) {
        while (true) {
            if (show.claim(seat, id)) return true;               // it was free
            String holder = show.claimant(seat);
            if (holder == null) continue;                        // freed: retry
            Booking other = bookings.get(holder);
            if (other != null && !other.tryExpire(clock.instant()))
                return false;                                    // live hold, or sold
            if (show.reclaim(seat, holder, id)) return true;     // CAS from the dead
        }
    }

    Booking confirm(String bookingId) {
        Booking b = get(bookingId);
        if (b.status() != BookingStatus.HELD) throw new IllegalStateException(b.id() + " is " + b.status());
        String ref = payments.charge(b.user(), b.amount());      // slow, may throw
        if (!b.tryConfirm(clock.instant(), ref)) {
            payments.refund(ref);
            throw new IllegalStateException("hold expired during payment, refunded " + ref);
        }
        return b;
    }

    void cancel(String bookingId) {
        Booking b = get(bookingId);
        if (b.cancel()) b.seats().forEach(s -> b.show().release(s, b.id()));
    }

    String seatMap(Show show) {
        StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
        char row = 0;
        for (Seat s : show.seats()) {
            if (s.row() != row) { out.append(row == 0 ? "" : "\n").append(s.row()).append(' '); row = s.row(); }
            String holder = show.claimant(s);
            Booking b = holder == null ? null : bookings.get(holder);
            out.append(b == null ? '.'
                     : b.status() == BookingStatus.CONFIRMED ? 'X'
                     : b.isLive(clock.instant()) ? 'h' : '.');
        }
        return out.toString();
    }

    private Booking get(String id) {
        Booking b = bookings.get(id);
        if (b == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no booking " + id);
        return b;
    }
}

final class MutableClock extends Clock {
    private volatile Instant now;
    MutableClock(Instant start) { now = start; }
    void advance(Duration d) { now = now.plus(d); }
    @Override public Instant instant() { return now; }
    @Override public ZoneId getZone() { return ZoneOffset.UTC; }
    @Override public Clock withZone(ZoneId zone) { throw new UnsupportedOperationException(); }
}
BookingDemo.java · 3 of 3 · the demo
public class BookingDemo {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        var clock = new MutableClock(Instant.parse("2026-10-03T13:00:00Z"));
        Duration[] slowNext = { Duration.ZERO };
        int[] refs = { 0 };
        PaymentGateway gateway = new PaymentGateway() {
            public String charge(String user, long amount) {
                clock.advance(slowNext[0]);               // a slow payment
                slowNext[0] = Duration.ZERO;
                return "PAY" + ++refs[0];
            }
            public void refund(String ref) { System.out.println("  refund " + ref); }
        };
        var service = new BookingService(new WeekendPricing(), gateway, clock);
        var show = new Show("S1", new Movie("Dune: Part Two", 166),
                LocalDateTime.of(2026, 10, 3, 19, 30),       // a Saturday
                new TreeMap<>(Map.of('A', SeatCategory.REGULAR, 'B', SeatCategory.PREMIUM,
                        'C', SeatCategory.RECLINER)), 5);

        Booking ana = service.hold("ana", show, List.of("A3", "A4")).orElseThrow();
        System.out.println("hold  " + ana);
        System.out.println("hold  bo A4,A5: " + service.hold("bo", show, List.of("A4", "A5"))
                .map(Booking::toString).orElse("refused, and A5 stays free"));

        var winners = new AtomicInteger();
        try (var pool = Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) {
            for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) {
                String user = "fan" + i;
                pool.submit(() -> service.hold(user, show, List.of("B2", "B1"))
                                         .ifPresent(b -> winners.incrementAndGet()));
            }
        }
        System.out.println("race  100 users for B1,B2: " + winners.get() + " hold");
        System.out.println(service.seatMap(show));

        System.out.println("pay   " + service.confirm(ana.id()));
        Booking cy = service.hold("cy", show, List.of("C1")).orElseThrow();
        clock.advance(Duration.ofMinutes(9));             // cy walks away
        System.out.println("hold  dee C1 after cy's hold ran out: "
                + service.hold("dee", show, List.of("C1")).map(Booking::toString).orElse("refused"));
        System.out.println("      cy's booking is now " + cy.status());

        Booking eve = service.hold("eve", show, List.of("C3")).orElseThrow();
        slowNext[0] = Duration.ofMinutes(10);
        try { service.confirm(eve.id()); }
        catch (IllegalStateException e) { System.out.println("pay   eve: " + e.getMessage()); }
        System.out.println(service.seatMap(show));
    }
}

Movie booking: the choices to defend, and the follow-ups to expect

Every follow-up on this problem is really "what if this runs on ten servers?" In-process atomics protect one JVM. Across servers, the same three operations (claim if free, take over if dead, release if mine) become conditional updates in a database or in Redis, and the design keeps its shape.

DecisionWhy, and the alternative
Per-seat atomic claimsNo lock, and holds on different seats never wait for each other. The alternative, synchronized on the show, is simpler and fine for one screen; it serialises every user on a hot release.
Claim in sorted orderTwo overlapping requests cannot each take half and both fail. Same rule as lock ordering.
Lazy expiryCorrect the instant a hold lapses, with no job to schedule or monitor. A sweeper can still tidy up.
Charge, then confirm, then refund if lateConfirming is instant and cannot fail except by expiry; charging is slow and can. The reverse order confirms seats that may never be paid for.
Booking-level lock for transitions"Confirm" and "expire" race on the same booking; a small lock makes exactly one win.
Facade serviceThe client calls hold and confirm; the claim protocol stays inside. See Facade.
The same protocol in SQLClaim: INSERT INTO seat_claim(show_id, seat, booking_id) … with a unique key on (show_id, seat); a duplicate-key error means taken. Take over a dead hold: UPDATE seat_claim SET booking_id=:new WHERE show_id=:s AND seat=:x AND booking_id=:old, and check that one row changed. Release: DELETE … WHERE booking_id=:mine. With Redis, SET seat:S1:B1 BK7 NX PX 480000 claims with a built-in expiry. See Distributed locks and leases.
Follow-upWhat changes
Payment callback arrives after a timeoutPayments are confirmed by a webhook, not a return value. Key the webhook by booking id; confirm or refund is decided by tryConfirm exactly as now, and a repeated webhook is ignored because the booking is no longer HELD.
Cancel a paid bookingA REFUND_PENDING state, a refund policy strategy (full refund up to 2 hours before the show), then release the seats.
No single empty seat between bookingsA SeatSelectionRule checked in hold before claiming. It reads the seat map, so it is advisory under concurrency; the claim is still the authority.
Dynamic pricingA PricingStrategy that reads occupancy. The price is fixed on the booking at hold time, so it cannot change during payment.
Coupons and offersDecorators around the pricing strategy, or a discount step in confirm with its own validation.
Live seat map for 10,000 viewersPublish claim and release events; clients subscribe over WebSockets. The map is a read model and can lag; the claim is what counts.
A virtual waiting room at release timeAdmit users in batches before they reach hold. This is a rate limiter in front of the service; see the token bucket.

Splitwise: exact arithmetic, four ways to split, and one real algorithm

Splitwise is a favourite machine-coding problem because it has a precise input format, an exact expected output, and a trap in every line: money that does not divide evenly, splits that do not add up, and debts that should net off against each other. It ends with the question every interviewer asks: "can you settle everyone with fewer payments?"

Functional requirements

  1. An expense has one payer, a total, and a split among participants (the payer may or may not be one).
  2. Split types: EQUAL; EXACT amounts, which must add up to the total; PERCENT, which must add up to 100; SHARES in a ratio (1:2).
  3. Amounts are rupees with paise. Shares must add up to the total to the paisa: ₹100 three ways is 33.34 + 33.33 + 33.33, with the extra paisa assigned by a fixed rule.
  4. Show balances: who owes whom, with debts in both directions between two people netted off.
  5. Settle up: record a payment from one user to another.
  6. Simplify: a list of payments that settles every balance, using as few payments as practical.
  7. Commands arrive as text lines, as in most machine-coding rounds: EXPENSE ana 1200.00 EQUAL ana bo cy.

Questions to ask first

Groups?
One global ledger here; groups are a follow-up.
Several payers?
One payer per expense. Several payers is a follow-up.
Currency?
One currency, two decimal places.
Rounding rule?
Split exactly, then give leftover paise to participants in the order listed.
Edit or delete an expense?
A follow-up: it needs the ledger to be rebuilt from expenses.

Nouns, and what they become

LedgerDebtSimplifier Expense · recordTransfer · record SplitRule · sealed, 4 recordsSplitRules · factory

Not classes here: user (a string id until users have profiles), group, currency. Balance is a map the ledger derives, never stored separately.

The first decision: never a double₹999.99 split 50/50 is 499.995 each. A double cannot represent either number exactly, and totals drift after a few hundred expenses. Store paise in a long, so all arithmetic is exact and the rounding rule is explicit. See value objects.

Splitwise: split rules compute shares, the ledger nets debts, the simplifier plans payments

The split types differ in how they turn a total into shares, and in what they validate, so each is its own record behind a sealed interface. Three of them are the same weighted split with different weights. The ledger keeps one netted debt per pair of people. The simplifier is a pure function from net balances to payments: a pure fabrication in GRASP terms, since no domain object owns it.

«sealed interface» SplitRule + shares(total) : Map<person, paise> sums to total ┄┄▷ «record» EqualSplit(people) weights 1, 1, 1 ┄┄▷ «record» ShareSplit(weights) weights 1, 2 ┄┄▷ «record» PercentSplit(percents) weights must sum to 100 ┄┄▷ «record» ExactSplit(amounts) must sum to total SplitRules factory + of(type, people, values) : SplitRule + byWeight(total, weights) : Map shared rounding rule Ledger - owes : Map<debtor, Map<creditor, paise>> netted - expenses : List<Expense> + add(payer, total, SplitRule) : Expense + settle(from, to, paise) + netBalances() : Map<person, paise> + debts() : List<Transfer> ◆── * Expense ┄┄> SplitRule DebtSimplifier pure function + simplify(netBalances) : List<Transfer> «record» Expense id, payer, total, shares «record» Transfer from, to, paise
ClassOwns the decision
Each SplitRuleIts validation, and how a total becomes shares
SplitRulesWhich rule a command means; the rounding rule every weighted split shares
LedgerRecording debts and netting them per pair
DebtSimplifierWhich payments settle a set of balances
Strategy, sealedEach split rule is a strategy, with one method. It is sealed because the set of split types is part of the product and the parser must handle all of them. A new type (split by nights stayed) is a new record, one factory case, and a compile error until both are written.
Net per pair, or net per person?The ledger keeps "bo owes ana 400" per pair, so the app can show each friendship. Per-person net balances are derived from it, and are all the simplifier needs. Storing both would mean two sources of truth that can drift apart.

Splitwise: four split rules, one rounding rule, and a factory that parses them

Equal, share and percent splits are all "divide by weight": give each person the floor of their share, then hand the leftover paise out one at a time in the order listed. Writing that once, in byWeight, means every split type rounds the same way and every result adds up exactly. Each record checks its own input in its compact constructor, so an invalid split cannot be created.

SplitwiseDemo.java · 1 of 3 · split rules and the factory
import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.*;

sealed interface SplitRule permits EqualSplit, ShareSplit, PercentSplit, ExactSplit {
    Map<String, Long> shares(long total);           // person -> paise, sums to total
}

record EqualSplit(List<String> people) implements SplitRule {
    EqualSplit {
        if (people.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("nobody to split with");
        people = List.copyOf(people);
    }
    public Map<String, Long> shares(long total) {
        Map<String, Long> ones = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        people.forEach(p -> ones.put(p, 1L));
        return SplitRules.byWeight(total, ones);
    }
}

record ShareSplit(Map<String, Long> weights) implements SplitRule {
    ShareSplit { weights = SplitRules.positive(weights); }
    public Map<String, Long> shares(long total) { return SplitRules.byWeight(total, weights); }
}

record PercentSplit(Map<String, Long> percents) implements SplitRule {
    PercentSplit {
        percents = SplitRules.positive(percents);
        long sum = percents.values().stream().mapToLong(Long::longValue).sum();
        if (sum != 100) throw new IllegalArgumentException("percents add up to " + sum);
    }
    public Map<String, Long> shares(long total) { return SplitRules.byWeight(total, percents); }
}

record ExactSplit(Map<String, Long> amounts) implements SplitRule {
    ExactSplit { amounts = SplitRules.positive(amounts); }
    public Map<String, Long> shares(long total) {
        long sum = amounts.values().stream().mapToLong(Long::longValue).sum();
        if (sum != total)                           // needs the total, so checked here
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("exact amounts add up to "
                    + Money.format(sum) + ", not " + Money.format(total));
        return amounts;
    }
}

final class SplitRules {                            // factory + shared rounding
    private SplitRules() {}

    static SplitRule of(String type, List<String> people, List<Long> values) {
        return switch (type) {
            case "EQUAL"   -> new EqualSplit(people);
            case "SHARES"  -> new ShareSplit(zip(people, values));
            case "PERCENT" -> new PercentSplit(zip(people, values));
            case "EXACT"   -> new ExactSplit(zip(people, values));
            default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("unknown split " + type);
        };
    }

    static Map<String, Long> byWeight(long total, Map<String, Long> weights) {
        long sum = weights.values().stream().mapToLong(Long::longValue).sum();
        Map<String, Long> out = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        long given = 0;
        for (var e : weights.entrySet()) {
            long share = Math.multiplyExact(total, e.getValue()) / sum;   // floor
            out.put(e.getKey(), share);
            given += share;
        }
        for (var e : out.entrySet()) {              // leftover paise, in order
            if (given == total) break;
            e.setValue(e.getValue() + 1);
            given++;
        }
        return Collections.unmodifiableMap(out);
    }

    static Map<String, Long> positive(Map<String, Long> m) {
        if (m.isEmpty() || m.values().stream().anyMatch(v -> v <= 0))
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("values must be positive");
        return Collections.unmodifiableMap(new LinkedHashMap<>(m));
    }

    private static Map<String, Long> zip(List<String> people, List<Long> values) {
        if (values.size() != people.size())
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("every person needs a value");
        Map<String, Long> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < people.size(); i++)
            if (m.put(people.get(i), values.get(i)) != null)
                throw new IllegalArgumentException(people.get(i) + " listed twice");
        return m;
    }
}

final class Money {
    private Money() {}
    static long parse(String rupees) {              // "999.99" -> 99999
        return new BigDecimal(rupees).movePointRight(2).longValueExact();
    }
    static String format(long paise) { return BigDecimal.valueOf(paise, 2).toPlainString(); }
}

record Expense(String id, String payer, long total, Map<String, Long> shares) {}
record Transfer(String from, String to, long amount) {
    @Override public String toString() { return from + " pays " + to + " " + Money.format(amount); }
}
byWeight(10000, {ana:1, bo:1, dee:1}) floor(10000 × 1 / 3) = 3333 for each given 9999, one paisa left ana 3334 bo 3333 dee 3333 sum 10000 byWeight(99999, {ana:50, dee:50}) floor(99999 × 50 / 100) = 49999 for each given 99998, one paisa left ana 50000 dee 49999 sum 99999
Why the leftover goes in listed orderAny fixed rule is fine, as long as the result adds up and the same input always gives the same output. "Leftover paise to the first people listed" is easy to explain and to test. The largest-remainder method is fairer for percentages; say so if asked, and note that it is a change to one method.
Where validation livesPercent totals are checked in the constructor, because the percentages alone decide validity. Exact amounts can only be checked against the expense total, so ExactSplit.shares checks it. Both reject input before the ledger changes.
The factory is the parser's only linkSplitRules.of maps the command word to a record. A new split type is a record plus one line here, and the exhaustive switch in any reporting code tells you what else to update.

Splitwise: netting debts per pair, simplifying them greedily, and a command-line run

Recording "bo owes ana 300" first cancels against any "ana owes bo" that already exists, so each pair of people has at most one debt. The simplifier ignores pairs entirely. It works from each person's net balance and repeatedly lets the biggest debtor pay the biggest creditor. Each payment settles at least one person, so n people never need more than n − 1 payments.

SplitwiseDemo.java · 2 of 3 · the ledger and the simplifier
final class Ledger {
    private final Map<String, Map<String, Long>> owes = new TreeMap<>();  // debtor -> creditor
    private final List<Expense> expenses = new ArrayList<>();

    synchronized Expense add(String payer, long total, SplitRule rule) {
        if (total <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("total must be positive");
        Map<String, Long> shares = rule.shares(total);           // validates first
        var e = new Expense("E" + (expenses.size() + 1), payer, total, shares);
        shares.forEach((person, share) -> {
            if (!person.equals(payer)) owe(person, payer, share);
        });
        expenses.add(e);
        return e;
    }

    synchronized void settle(String from, String to, long amount) {
        if (amount <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("amount must be positive");
        owe(to, from, amount);                     // a payment is a debt reversed
    }

    private void owe(String debtor, String creditor, long amount) {
        long reverse = owes.getOrDefault(creditor, Map.of()).getOrDefault(debtor, 0L);
        long offset = Math.min(reverse, amount);   // cancel the opposite debt first
        adjust(creditor, debtor, -offset);
        adjust(debtor, creditor, amount - offset);
    }

    private void adjust(String debtor, String creditor, long delta) {
        if (delta == 0) return;
        Map<String, Long> row = owes.computeIfAbsent(debtor, k -> new TreeMap<>());
        if (row.merge(creditor, delta, Long::sum) == 0) row.remove(creditor);
        if (row.isEmpty()) owes.remove(debtor);
    }

    synchronized List<Transfer> debts() {
        List<Transfer> out = new ArrayList<>();
        owes.forEach((d, row) -> row.forEach((c, amt) -> out.add(new Transfer(d, c, amt))));
        return out;
    }

    synchronized Map<String, Long> netBalances() {                 // + is owed
        Map<String, Long> net = new TreeMap<>();
        owes.forEach((d, row) -> row.forEach((c, amt) -> {
            net.merge(c, amt, Long::sum);
            net.merge(d, -amt, Long::sum);
        }));
        return net;
    }
}

final class DebtSimplifier {
    private record Party(String who, long amount) {}

    static List<Transfer> simplify(Map<String, Long> net) {
        Comparator<Party> biggestFirst = Comparator.comparingLong(Party::amount)
                .reversed().thenComparing(Party::who);             // ties: by name
        var creditors = new PriorityQueue<>(biggestFirst);
        var debtors = new PriorityQueue<>(biggestFirst);
        net.forEach((who, amt) -> {
            if (amt > 0) creditors.add(new Party(who, amt));
            if (amt < 0) debtors.add(new Party(who, -amt));
        });
        List<Transfer> out = new ArrayList<>();
        while (!creditors.isEmpty() && !debtors.isEmpty()) {
            Party c = creditors.poll(), d = debtors.poll();
            long amt = Math.min(c.amount(), d.amount());
            out.add(new Transfer(d.who(), c.who(), amt));           // one settles fully
            if (c.amount() > amt) creditors.add(new Party(c.who(), c.amount() - amt));
            if (d.amount() > amt) debtors.add(new Party(d.who(), d.amount() - amt));
        }
        return out;
    }
}
SplitwiseDemo.java · 3 of 3 · the command runner
public class SplitwiseDemo {
    static final Ledger ledger = new Ledger();

    static void run(String line) {
        System.out.println("> " + line);
        String[] t = line.trim().split("\\s+");
        try {
            switch (t[0]) {
                case "EXPENSE" -> {                 // EXPENSE payer total TYPE args
                    List<String> people = new ArrayList<>();
                    List<Long> values = new ArrayList<>();
                    for (int i = 4; i < t.length; i++) {
                        String[] kv = t[i].split("=");
                        people.add(kv[0]);
                        if (kv.length == 2)
                            values.add(t[3].equals("EXACT") ? Money.parse(kv[1]) : Long.parseLong(kv[1]));
                    }
                    var e = ledger.add(t[1], Money.parse(t[2]), SplitRules.of(t[3], people, values));
                    var parts = new StringJoiner(", ");
                    e.shares().forEach((p, s) -> parts.add(p + " " + Money.format(s)));
                    System.out.println("  " + e.id() + " shares: " + parts);
                }
                case "SETTLE" -> ledger.settle(t[1], t[2], Money.parse(t[3]));
                case "SHOW" -> ledger.debts().forEach(d -> System.out.println(
                        "  " + d.from() + " owes " + d.to() + " " + Money.format(d.amount())));
                case "SIMPLIFY" -> DebtSimplifier.simplify(ledger.netBalances())
                        .forEach(x -> System.out.println("  " + x));
                default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("unknown command " + t[0]);
            }
        } catch (IllegalArgumentException | ArithmeticException e) {
            System.out.println("  error: " + e.getMessage());
        }
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        """
        EXPENSE ana 1200.00 EQUAL ana bo cy
        EXPENSE bo 1000.00 EXACT ana=300.00 bo=200.00 cy=500.00
        EXPENSE cy 999.99 PERCENT ana=50 dee=50
        EXPENSE dee 100.00 EQUAL ana bo dee
        EXPENSE ana 600.00 SHARES bo=1 cy=2
        EXPENSE ana 500.00 EXACT bo=100.00 cy=100.00
        EXPENSE ana 500.00 PERCENT bo=60 cy=30
        SHOW
        SIMPLIFY
        SETTLE cy ana 300.00
        SHOW
        """.lines().forEach(SplitwiseDemo::run);
    }
}
